items.stem: When interpreting an lm() summary from observational data, why is caution needed with coefficients?

options.text: An association in observational data does not establish causation
options.rationale: Confounding and design limits mean coefficients are not inherently causal.

options.text: Coefficients from lm are always exactly zero
options.rationale: They are estimated values, not always zero.

options.text: lm cannot be used on observational data
options.rationale: It can; the caution is about interpretation.
Fit quality does not establish causation.

items.explanation: Confounding and design limits mean coefficients are not inherently causal.

items.stem: Select TWO practices that improve reproducibility of an R analysis.

options.text: Setting a random seed before stochastic steps
options.rationale: A fixed seed makes random results repeatable.

options.text: Pinning package versions with a tool like renv
options.rationale: Recording exact dependency versions stabilises results across machines.

options.text: Relying on the interactive global environment state
Hardcoding absolute paths to your home directory

items.stem: Why can growing a vector inside a loop (e.g. x <- c(x, i)) be slow in R?

options.text: Each append can copy the whole vector due to copy-on-modify, giving quadratic cost
options.rationale: Repeated reallocation and copying makes incremental growth expensive; preallocation avoids it.
Loops are allowed; the issue is repeated copying.
c() returns a vector here; the cost is copying.
Growth does not change the type to a factor.

items.explanation: Repeated reallocation and copying makes incremental growth expensive; preallocation avoids it.
